Baugh holds two meetings to plan the operation against the Steiners, including online harassment and disturbing deliveries.

description: Threatening messages, disturbing deliveries, Craigslist posts and related intimidation target the Steiners.
Team travels to Natick and attempts to install a GPS tracker on the Steiners' vehicle, followed by surveillance and following them by car.
Steiners report the activity; NPD investigation begins.
eBay begins internal investigation after contact from Natick police.
Baugh texts Wymer that his team 'ran an op' in Boston while assuring him no crime was committed; security-team members also obstruct investigations.

description: eBay places Baugh, Popp and Harville on leave and later terminates them, Gilbert and Stockwell; Zea's contract is terminated. Wymer is terminated for cause; board requests Wenig resignation in September.
Federal prosecutors charge members of the former eBay security team; Cooke becomes the seventh charged participant.
Cooke, Gilbert, Popp, Stockwell, Zea, Baugh and Harville plead guilty in the criminal cases.
outcome: All seven prosecuted participants ultimately plead guilty.
